agent_response.summary: Candidate 2 builds on candidate 1. It replaces the single dense 751×751 LU per frequency with a block/Schur factorization. The signal matrix's upper/lower sideband cross blocks are structural zeros per the source trace (build.py:177-266, 813-825, 1373-1374). So A = [[diag(B1,B2), Q],[R, M]] is factored as two 286×286 LUs, W = P⁻¹Q, and an LU of the 179×179 Schur complement S = M − R W. All three signal-system solves (signal, A^H noise weights, covariances) reuse these factors through the same lax.custom_linear_solve wrapper. The matvec and derivative structure are unchanged; the trans 0/1/2 solves use A = [[P,0],[R,S]]·[[I,W],[0,I]]. Candidate 1 results are recorded in experiments/notes/claude-linear-algebra.md: first run 31.509 s vs 35.737 s baseline, warm 10.88 s, official checks pass, strict array check fails on 3 gradient entries (max relative 1.5e-6).
agent_response.hypothesis: After candidate 1 the forward pass (7.9 s warm) is dominated by one batch of 101 complex 751-LUs, about 4.5 s judging by candidate 1's saving. The block factorization needs about 1.1e8 complex FMA per frequency vs 2.8e8 for a dense LU. That should cut forward runtime by roughly 2–3 s, and the first run by a similar amount, while the gradient stage and compile time stay about the same. Because pivoting is now restricted to within blocks, numerical differences may be larger than candidate 1's. Carrier and powers should remain identical; signal, noise and gradient will differ at rounding level unless B1, B2 or S is ill-conditioned.
agent_response.notes: Candidate 1 (3db9b657) measured: screen af18c374… 31.429 s; full cd271462… 31.509 s first run, warm median 10.876 s, peak RSS 12.48 GB. Official checks passed (|Δlog sens| 5.37e-6, FD check ok). Strict comparison: carrier, signal and powers bitwise identical; noise relative L2 error 2.2e-8; gradient failed at idx 33/161/180 (relative 3e-7, 1.5e-6, 2.3e-7). The cause is pivoting from LU(A)^H vs LU(A^H). The maintainer needs to decide whether this tolerance is acceptable. Candidate 2 is unexecuted locally (no runtime in this launcher), and the zero cross blocks are a source-derived claim not verified at runtime. What to check: whether the screen traces and passes; forward time vs candidate 1's 7.94 s; and the size of the noise, signal and gradient diffs vs the baseline and vs candidate 1. If the sensitivity check fails or diffs grow by orders of magnitude, reject candidate 2 and keep candidate 1 as the best speed result. Possible follow-ups: exploit the sparsity of B1/B2 (not yet measured), or check the remaining compile time (forward compile ~13 s), which is a bigger share now and overlaps the seed agent's dispatch work.
